(FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote) 19/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

20/ On or before June 30, 2027, the state treasurer shall report to the joint legislative budget committee staff on the state treasurer's current fiscal year and estimated next fiscal year expenditures of interest earnings spent pursuant to sections 35-315 and 35-318, Arizona Revised Statutes, for the state treasurer's banking service contract, external investment management agreement, administrative and information technology costs and any other costs. (General Appropriations Act footnote).

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$4,721,600 and 38.4 FTE Positions in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts consist of:

General Fund \$342,500

State Treasurer’s Operating Fund 4,379,100

These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Advanced Air Mobility Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Advanced Air Mobility Fund. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(2,000,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for a deposit into the Advanced Air Mobility Fund.

The FY 2026 Transportation Budget Reconciliation Bill (BRB) established a new appropriated Advanced Air Mobility Fund. Monies in the fund will be used to purchase advanced air mobility vehicles capable of carrying passengers or cargo to demonstrate the utility of such vehicles. Monies in the fund may also be used to construct vertiports, which are commonly defined as areas designated for the takeoff and landing of these vehicles. The FY 2026 budget included a footnote appropriating the deposited monies from the fund to the State Treasurer for the fund's aforementioned purpose.

Secure Ballot Paper

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Secure Ballot Paper. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026

Laws 2022, Chapter 313, Section 130 appropriated \$5,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2024 and \$6,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2025 to the Treasurer to distribute these monies on a proportional basis to county recorders that purchase ballot paper that uses specific security features, including watermarks or unique ballot identifiers, or both. Monies in this line item are exempt from lapsing.

Justice of the Peace Salaries

The Baseline includes \$2,797,200 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Justice of the Peace (JP) salaries. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

A.R.S. § 22-117 requires the state to pay 40% of the salary for each Justice of the Peace, with the county paying the remainder. This provision does not apply to Maricopa County, which pays 100% of its JP costs. A.R.S. § 22-117 also limits the amount that the state can reimburse to the counties to the amount appropriated.

Justice of the Peace salaries are based on a proportion of the annual compensation for a Superior Court judge as determined by the guidelines for Judicial Productivity Credits (JPCs) outlined in statute. JPCs are calculated every year and are based on the total and type of cases that a Justice of the Peace hears and whether the Justice receives clerical help. An annual average JPC total is compared against the salary ranges in statute to determine an individual Justice’s compensation.

Law Enforcement/Boating Safety Fund Grants

The Baseline includes \$2,183,800 from the Law Enforcement and Boating Safety Fund (LEBSF) in FY 2027 for the administration of the Law Enforcement/Boating Safety Fund grants. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

A.R.S. § 5-383 requires the State Treasurer to administer LEBSF monies. However, the allocation determinations are made by the Arizona Game and Fish Commission. The Treasurer disburses monies to county law enforcement agencies in Apache, Coconino, Gila, La Paz, Maricopa, Mohave, Navajo, and Yuma Counties in accordance with the distribution formula developed by the Arizona Game and Fish Commission. The FY 2024 and FY 2025 allocations are included in Table 1.

Special Sporting Event

The Baseline includes \$1,500,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Special Sporting Event funding. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item are used to promote an auto racing sporting event. The Office of Tourism is required to provide an annual report on or before October 1 to the JLBC that includes the amounts and purposes of all expenditures made from these monies in the previous fiscal year. Because this authorization is in permanent statute, the appropriation amount is not included in the General Appropriations Act.

A.R.S. § 41-2308 requires the Treasurer to send \$125,000 each month (for an annual total of \$1,500,000) to the Office of Tourism through FY 2051 for special sporting event promotions. (For more background, see the FY 2023 Appropriations Report.)

Statewide Infrastructure Trust Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Statewide Infrastructure Trust Fund. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,000,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for a deposit into the Statewide Infrastructure Trust Fund.

The FY 2026 Transportation BRB established a new appropriated Statewide Infrastructure Trust Fund. Monies in the fund will be used to finance projects that construct or improve federal or state highways. All expenditures from the fund are subject to review by the Joint Committee on Capital Review. The FY 2026 budget included a footnote appropriating the deposited monies from the fund to the State Treasurer for the fund's aforementioned purpose.

Statewide Transportation Innovation Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Statewide Transportation Innovation Fund. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(2,000,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for a deposit into the Statewide Transportation Innovation Fund.

The FY 2026 Transportation BRB established a new appropriated Statewide Transportation Innovation Fund. Monies in the fund will be used to administer the Statewide Transportation Innovation Program established pursuant to A.R.S. § 28-9572. The FY 2026 budget included a footnote appropriating the deposited monies from the fund to the State Treasurer for the fund's aforementioned purpose.

Veteran's Health Innovations Pilot Program

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Veterans' Health Innovations Pilot Program. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(150,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for a Veterans' Health Innovations Pilot Program.

Monies in this line item will be allocated to a nonprofit charitable organization to conduct a pilot program with an emphasis on innovations that improve veterans' health. The monies will be allocated in accordance with A.R.S. § 41-177 subsection E, which establishes the guidelines for distributions from the Arizona Health Innovation Trust Fund.
